correctness.rationale: For all common-rate two-state generators, direct multiplication gives \(Q(a,b)Q(c,d)=-(a+b)Q(c,d)\); hence each exponential is affine in its generator and the ordered product has the exact form proved in RESULT.md. The two off-diagonal entries have sum \(1-e^{-hs}<1\), so entrywise nonnegativity is equivalent to two explicit off-diagonal inequalities. The positive coefficient stays positive, while the other changes sign exactly at \(hs=2\log(7+4\sqrt3)\). Reversed one-way generators establish necessity and small positive perturbations establish irreducible sharpness. Beyond the cutoff, the inequalities reduce to the two necessary-and-sufficient rate-ratio bounds. The standalone verifier checks algebraic identities over \(\mathbb Q(\sqrt3)\) and 4096 seeded numerical instances, but finite tests do not replace universal proof. Quantifiers and boundaries: \(h>0\), \(s>0\), \(a_j,b_j\ge0\), with \(a_j+b_j=s\) for both matrices.

value.rationale: The primary article singles out quantifying near-positivity for commutator-free schemes as an open methodological issue. Two-state Markov exchange with equal total rates is a natural basic class where both generator orientations can vary independently while the relaxation timescale is fixed. An exact sharp universal endpoint positivity threshold and a complete beyond-threshold rate condition identify when non-generator internal stages can still deliver a valid stochastic update; the irreducible counterexample proves the boundary is real. This goes beyond a parameter substitution or generic textbook sign test because the negative internal stages cancel nontrivially in the noncommuting product and the result precisely classifies a meaningful numerical-reliability regime. It is not an assertion about the entire nonlinear algorithm.
